title: Explainable AI Ranking of LSD Macro-Dynamics
takeaway: The thesis is a mechanism-ranking framework, not a claim that AI discovers the true biological mechanism of LSD.
bullets: Question: which transparent control-theoretic and graph-dynamic surrogate mechanisms align best with paired LSD-placebo fMRI proxy evidence?
Current result: C hierarchy/routing ranks first; E network-control energy ranks second; B DMDc is a negative baseline.
Defense stance: every claim is macro-dynamics proxy evidence, not receptor-level, clinical, or subjective-state validation.
speaker_notes: Open by narrowing the claim. This is not a psychedelic-experience simulator and not receptor pharmacology.
The project is valuable because it turns vague mechanism language into explicit, testable ranking hypotheses.

title: Why This Is A Thesis Instead Of A Demo
takeaway: The scientific contribution is the testing framework: mechanisms can win, lose, or fail honestly.
bullets: Prediction framing: rank candidate mechanism layers by signed alignment with empirical LSD-minus-placebo target summaries.
Explainability framing: each layer maps to named metrics, nulls, code paths, and limitations.
Scientific value: negative results are not hidden; they identify underconstrained or wrong mechanism stories.
speaker_notes: A reviewer will ask what is new. The answer is not a new brain theory; it is an auditable mechanism-ranking pipeline with explicit failure criteria.

title: Data Boundary
takeaway: The current empirical layer uses cached paired ds003059 placebo/LSD records; run-02 music is not part of the primary ranking yet.
bullets: Current input: 30 paired subject/run records from 15 subjects.
Current runs: run-01 and run-03.
Current representation: coarse 8-module time series and derived FC/state summaries.
Blocked claim: run-02/music remains exploratory until motion/context checks are completed.
speaker_notes: Say exactly what data are in the result. Do not imply external validation or music-run evidence.

title: Pipeline Overview
takeaway: The repo moves from cached fMRI summaries to mechanism scores, exports, and an interactive dashboard.
bullets: Load paired empirical records.
Compute A/B/C/D/E mechanism layers.
Rank mechanisms by signed support scores.
Export JSON, CSV, XLSX, HTML figures, report, and dashboard payload.
Use tests and smoke checks to protect reproducibility.
speaker_notes: This slide is the backbone for the rest of the deck. Every later slide maps to one stage of this flow.

title: Current Mechanism Ranking
takeaway: C and E are the current story; B is explicitly negative.
bullets: 1: C hierarchy/routing, score 0.332606.
2: E network-control energy, score 0.175078.
3: D dynamic repertoire / graph metrics, score 0.150619.
4: A transition-state proxy, score 0.148906.
5: B DMDc condition-interaction, score -0.074064.
speaker_notes: Do not overstate the differences between D and A; they are close. Emphasize that C is the clearest current leader and E is the control-theory candidate.

title: A: Transition-State Proxy
takeaway: A tests whether LSD broadens or destabilizes macro-state switching, but state labels are still a sensitivity risk.
bullets: Metrics: state occupancy entropy, transition entropy, transition rate, dwell time, barrier-reduction proxy, step distance.
Current evidence: weak-to-moderate support through transition entropy, transition rate, and shorter dwell proxies.
Main caveat: PCA-quantile state labels are transparent but not a final HMM/state-space solution.
speaker_notes: Use this as an interpretable baseline layer. It motivates state dynamics, but it is not enough for final mechanism claims.

title: B: DMDc Predictive Baseline
takeaway: B does not support the main story, and that makes the result more defensible.
bullets: Equation: z_pair(x[t+1]) = A z_pair(x[t]) + B u[t] + C(u[t] * z_pair(x[t])) + bias + noise.
Validation: leave-one-subject-out one-step prediction.
Result: condition-interaction relative improvement is -0.074064 percent.
Interpretation: DMDc is a negative-control baseline, not network-control energy.
speaker_notes: This is a defense strength: the project does not hide that simple linear prediction is weak.

title: C: Hierarchy And Routing
takeaway: C is the strongest current layer because sensory, thalamic, and receptor-prior coupling signs align best.
bullets: Supportive: sensory-transmodal coupling, sensory global coupling, thalamic global/transmodal coupling.
Added upgrade: hierarchy-gradient flattening and receptor-weighted global coupling.
Sign conflict: associative-global coupling does not match the expected direction.
Claim boundary: this is FC proxy evidence, not proof of REBUS or thalamic gating.
speaker_notes: This is the slide to linger on. It carries the current thesis-ready result, but the conflict must be shown.

title: D: Dynamic Repertoire And Graph Metrics
takeaway: D improves after graph-theory metrics are added, but dynamic-FC movement remains mixed.
bullets: Supportive: between-network integration, modularity reduction, participation coefficient, global efficiency.
Weak/conflicting: dynamic-FC variance and FC path length move against the expected repertoire direction.
Next test: window-size sensitivity and dynamic-community robustness.
speaker_notes: Make clear that D is useful but not clean. It adds network neuroscience credibility without becoming the headline.

title: E: Network-Control Energy
takeaway: E is the mathematically serious control-theory layer, but it is still a proxy until structural connectomes and PET receptor maps are added.
bullets: Equation: x[t+1] = A_graph x[t] + B_profile u[t].
Energy: minimum finite-horizon sum of squared control inputs.
Profiles: receptor, hierarchy, sensory, transmodal, thalamic, uniform, degree, random receptor-prior permutations.
Current graph: macro-module proxy graph, not a structural connectome.
speaker_notes: Explain E intuitively: how much control effort is needed to move from one brain-state summary to another under a chosen control profile.

title: E Result: Supportive But Split
takeaway: E supports lower LSD transition energy, but not receptor-specific control placement.
bullets: Supportive: LSD vs placebo receptor-profile transition-energy reduction is +4.70 percent.
Supportive: LSD vs placebo uniform-control transition-energy reduction is +6.94 percent.
Not supportive: receptor-prior control is -34.39 percent worse than uniform control.
Not supportive: receptor-prior control is -15.08 percent worse than random receptor-prior permutations.
Defensible claim: landscape-flattening proxy is plausible; receptor-specific placement remains unproven.
speaker_notes: This is probably the most important defense slide. It prevents overclaiming while preserving the control-theory contribution.

title: File-By-File Code Walkthrough
takeaway: The project is explainable because the code has a clear path from data to metrics to exports.
bullets: Data loading: empirical viewer JSON records become paired placebo/LSD arrays.
Metric engine: dynamic_mechanism.py computes A+B+C+D+E.
Artifact engine: run_dynamic_mechanism_ranking.py writes report, tables, and figures.
Export engine: export_dynamic_mechanism_tables.py creates reviewable CSV/XLSX files.
Demo layer: FastAPI app and dashboard template expose results interactively.
Tests: focused tests assert schema, dashboard containers, and parcellation metadata.
speaker_notes: Use this slide to show that the project is not a black box. Every result has a function, file, and artifact.

title: How The Code Runs
takeaway: The demo can be reproduced with a short command chain and audited through saved artifacts.
bullets: Run ranking: uv run python scripts/run_dynamic_mechanism_ranking.py
Export review tables: uv run python scripts/export_dynamic_mechanism_tables.py
Launch dashboard: uv run python scripts/run_dashboard.py
Primary outputs: summary.json, stage report, HTML figures, CSV/XLSX workbook.

speaker_notes: Do not promise full pytest is currently clean if the environment still has temp/coverage permission problems.

title: Explainability Plan
takeaway: Explainability here means traceable mechanisms, signed metrics, nulls, and failure modes rather than post-hoc mysticism.
bullets: Global explanation: mechanism ranking board and layer scores.
Metric explanation: signed effect size, sign consistency, sign-test p-values.
Individual failure explanation: metric-level sign conflicts and negative baselines.
Control explanation: compare receptor, uniform, random, degree, and future structural nulls.
Presentation explanation: show what each layer would need to support before a claim strengthens.
speaker_notes: Avoid making SHAP the center of this project. The current explainability is stronger because the mechanism layers are themselves interpretable.

title: Robustness Is The Next Scientific Gate
takeaway: The next thesis task is not a prettier deck; it is proving whether C and E survive stress tests.
bullets: Subject/bootstrap uncertainty for layer scores.
Run split: run-01 vs run-03.
E horizon sensitivity.
A/E state-labeling sensitivity.
D window-size sensitivity.
Decision: keep, weaken, or reject each mechanism story based on robustness.
speaker_notes: This slide answers what you would do next and shows you understand the current evidence is not final.

title: Hard Reviewer Questions
takeaway: The deck should make objections easy to answer before they are asked.
bullets: Why this model? Because every mechanism is explicit, testable, and falsifiable.
Why trust it? Trust the pipeline and artifacts, not a biological overclaim.
What is new? AI-assisted ranking and failure analysis of transparent control-theoretic surrogate mechanisms.
What is weak? 8-module proxy, coarse receptor priors, no structural connectome yet, motion sensitivity, dynamic-FC sensitivity.
What would change your mind? Robustness failure or nulls defeating C/E.
speaker_notes: This should be delivered plainly. Do not sound defensive; the limitations are part of the scientific design.

title: Demo Script
takeaway: The dashboard should be used as an evidence console, not a marketing page.
bullets: Open dashboard and show claim boundary first.
Show mechanism ranking board: C first, E second, B negative.
Open E plot and explain split result.
Open CSV/XLSX exports to show reviewability.
Show code path from dynamic_mechanism.py to dashboard payload.
End with next-step robustness gate.
speaker_notes: Keep the demo short. If the audience is skeptical, go straight to limitations and exports.

title: Thesis-Ready Claim
takeaway: The final claim is conservative, but it is defensible.
bullets: Current defensible claim: hierarchy/routing and graph-control-energy summaries align better with paired LSD-placebo macro-dynamic evidence than generic DMDc condition prediction.
Current unresolved claim: receptor-specific network-control placement remains unproven.
Minimum viable thesis: explainable mechanism ranking plus honest failure analysis.
Ambitious thesis: structural-connectome and PET-informed network-control robustness.
speaker_notes: End by showing that the project can succeed even if receptor-specific E remains negative.

title: What I Would Do Next
takeaway: Do robustness before structural upgrades or final slides.
bullets: 1. Run A+B+C+D+E robustness.
2. Upgrade E with a structural-connectome graph.
3. Upgrade receptor priors with PET-derived 5-HT2A maps.
4. Run Schaefer/Yeo sensitivity for C/D.
5. Build final defense deck after the robustness story stabilizes.
